style_prompt:
### DIRECTOR'S NOTES
Style: warm, grounded and genuinely curious, an Alaska public radio host who finds this interesting rather than impressive. Admire the work and stay level about what has not been measured yet. Dry, concrete honesty, never celebratory, never sour, never a gotcha.
Pace: MEASURED and unhurried. THIS IS A TWO MINUTE PIECE, about one hundred and twenty seconds, and the read must FILL it, so give every sentence room to land and take a real breath at every period. Do not rush the numbers. Vary the tone line to line so no two sentences sound the same.
Emphasis: lean on the key word in each line; let numbers land.
Delivery: let the short lines sit in silence rather than hurrying into the next one. Quiet and personal on "Remember them." The lines of figures are not a list: change cadence inside each one, state a count, then set the next number down separately. Settle down onto "a bad forecast costs gallons" rather than pushing it. Lift through the August award and the digital twin, then let "Four partners" arrive smaller and calmer, as a fair correction and not as a catch. Turn the corner audibly on "Now, those servers." Hand the Richard Wies line over as something he said. Widen and quiet down for the rest of Alaska. Speak the last two lines to one person in the room.

lines.text: In Cordova, Alaska, [curious] servers run inside a hydroelectric powerhouse.
lines.pace: baseline, concrete, no announcer lift
lines.why: The picture is surprising on its own, so the read stays flat and factual and lets the image pull; the single [curious] cue sits after the place name, where the surprise actually starts.

lines.text: Greensparc put a hundred seventy kilowatts there in twenty twenty four, cooled by turbine water.
lines.pace: baseline, let the kilowatt figure land, then lift slightly into the last three words
lines.why: The cooling detail is the best image in the opening, so it gets the hook's only real lift, and that lift buys the fall that line two needs.

lines.text: Remember them.
lines.pace: slow, a full beat before and after
lines.why: A direct instruction to one listener, so it drops out of narration into something quieter and more personal than anything around it; the four to one fall is the read's first real contrast.

lines.text: Cordova Electric runs an island grid. [short pause] Eighteen megawatts, fifteen sixty six customers, no wire out.
lines.pace: plain on the first sentence, then step DOWN through the three facts, the last one flattest and final
lines.why: The mechanism starts here and wants no colour, but three figures in a row will flatten if they are read at one pitch, so the pause separates the claim from the evidence and the run descends instead of listing.

lines.text: About eighty percent hydro, from two creeks. [slow] Ten point eight megawatts of diesel behind it.
lines.pace: warmer and easier on the two creeks, then slower and cooler on the diesel figure
lines.why: Two opposed resources, read below the line before so the split lands as arithmetic rather than drama; [slow] sits mid-line at a genuine change of cadence, which keeps the second figure from being swallowed by the first.

lines.text: Guess demand wrong and the co op can't buy from a neighbor. It burns fuel.
lines.pace: baseline through the clause, then a real beat before the short second sentence
lines.why: This is where the consequence bites, so it steps up out of the flattest line in the piece; 'burns' is the frame the fuel should hit on.

lines.text: So here, a bad forecast costs gallons.
lines.pace: slow and deliberate, weight by settling rather than pushing, land it and stop
lines.why: The thesis and the piece's first real weight. It earns that by dropping underneath the line before, which is the dry level honesty the angle asks for, and the low landing gives the August news somewhere to rise from.

lines.text: In August, U A F said it won seven hundred twenty five thousand from the Genesis Mission.
lines.pace: warmer colour, letters of U A F spoken separately and unhurried, the figure allowed to land whole
lines.why: Genuinely good news and the start of the only rise in the film; 'won' sits directly before the number and drives the figure without the narrator sounding impressed by it.

lines.text: AURORA A I is a digital twin of Cordova, built from the co op's records, with machine learning.
lines.pace: brightest line in the read but not faster, small breath at each comma, the letters A and I clearly separate
lines.why: The most interesting information in the film and the crest of the arc, which is exactly what makes the two step deflation that follows work.

lines.text: A Phase One award, beginning October first, nine months.
lines.pace: cooling off, each clause set down separately, the last two words plainest
lines.why: The clock. Reading it as three separate deposits rather than one phrase starts the descent from the crest without editorialising about the schedule.

lines.text: Four partners. U A F's share, three hundred twenty five thousand.
lines.pace: slow, even, a beat after the first sentence, no lean and no irony on the smaller number
lines.why: A smaller number arriving right after a bigger one, and it must sound like a correction offered in good faith. Any lift or edge here turns it into a gotcha, so the level falls and the delivery stays flat.

lines.text: Now, those servers.
lines.pace: a clear beat before it, then turn the corner audibly, brighter than anything since the twin
lines.why: A pivot, and it has to sound like one; the beat comes from silence rather than a tag because a tag can never open a line.

lines.text: Not the project's. Just a load on the same grid.
lines.pace: flat and corrective, both sentences the same weight
lines.why: The mandatory honesty beat about the two halves not being linked, read as a correction of the record and never as a wink.

lines.text: Whatever it predicts, it predicts them too.
lines.pace: baseline, lean on the last two words, this is the hook's promise being paid
lines.why: The payoff of 'Remember them.' The picture plugs the servers into the grid on 'them', so the emphasis has to be exactly there.

lines.text: So the test is narrow. [short pause] By June, gallons saved, or a demonstration?
lines.pace: measured, the question genuinely open at the end, no rhetorical dip
lines.why: The honest heart. The question is asked straight, and the pause holds open the empty measured slot the image shows here.

lines.text: Richard Wies, who leads it, calls that a really short period of performance.
lines.pace: slower, handed over rather than asserted, the closing phrase set slightly apart as his words
lines.why: It must sound QUOTED. The level drops and the narrator reports his phrase rather than agreeing with it out loud, which is what keeps the honesty from becoming an opinion.

lines.text: And Cordova is the easy case.
lines.pace: level, almost offhand, then stop
lines.why: A cold turn delivered without relish; saying it plainly is what makes the widening that follows land.

lines.text: Alaska's power cost program covers a hundred ninety three diesel communities, eighty two thousand people.
lines.pace: slow on both figures, a breath at the comma, the last two words wider and unhurried
lines.why: Two counts in one line, and the second is the one that means something; widening on 'people' turns a statistic into a place without raising the volume.

lines.text: They need it most, with the least data.
lines.pace: quietest line in the film, set the second clause down carefully
lines.why: The emotional low point in stakes rather than in volume; the read gets smaller so the sting is stated instead of sold.

lines.text: So watch for gallons.
lines.pace: clean and direct, a real beat before it
lines.why: The instruction the whole film exists to give, and the third time 'gallons' carries the throughline, so it is the one line that steps up out of the low stretch.

lines.text: What would convince you it worked?
lines.pace: slow, warm, to one person, no bright upward host lilt
lines.why: A real question to a real person, so it settles back down and stays conversational; an engagement-bait lilt here would undo the whole register.
